newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise after holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise after holiday weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices moved higher Monday as buyers re-emerged after the holiday weekend, market sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about two cents higher at $2.12-2.14 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub as temperatures along the Gulf Coast eased back into the low-90s F.
Traders blamed the uptick on a strong demand in the West, particularly in the California markets, where storage levels were still behind year-ago levels and some nuclear power was absent.

The 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit restarted and was operating at 50 percent power, but restart of the 1,080 MW San Onofre 2 unit was delayed one week to July 17. The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, was slated to restart July 12, according to the company.

Permian prices regained 11 cents to about $2.00-2.02 as California buyers came out in droves early today for additional supplies. As a result of increased demand, southern California border prices rose an average of eight cents to $2.15-2.20.
San Juan prices also staged significant gains to the low-to-mid $1.90s for constrained gas, up more than 10 cents from last Thursday.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate inched a couple of cents higher to the mid-to-high $2.30s despite cooler weather in the region.

In the Midwest, swing prices remained in the high-$1.90s. Chicago city-gate was also talked little changed around $2.16 as temperature highs were forecast in the high-70s F today in the region. Slightly warmer weather is forecast for Tuesday, but the 70s F are expected to return Wednesday, according to Weather Services Corp.
